binders: There exists a real number C.
Universally quantify over every real number p.
hypotheses: The witness C is strictly positive: 0 < C.
For the universally quantified exponent p, assume 1 <= p.
conclusions: For every real p >= 1, (integral over gaussianReal(0,1) of |x|^p)^(1/p) <= C * sqrt(p).
mathematical_definitions: The integral is the real-valued Bochner integral with respect to the measure gaussianReal(0,1) on the Borel real line.
Both powers use real exponentiation Real.rpow: the integrand is |x|^p and the outer exponent is the real reciprocal 1/p.
Absolute value is the usual real absolute value, and sqrt is the nonnegative real square root.
gaussianReal(0,1) is the nondegenerate Gaussian measure obtained from the gaussianPDF density with real location parameter 0 and nonnegative parameter 1.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a single positive real constant C such that, for every real exponent p at least 1, the 1/p real power of the Gaussian integral of |x|^p under gaussianReal(0,1) is at most C times the square root of p. The same C must work uniformly for all such p.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The exponent p ranges over real numbers satisfying p >= 1, not merely integers or natural numbers.
The constant C is existentially chosen before p and is therefore uniform in p; it is explicitly required to be strictly positive.
Because p >= 1, division by p in the exponent 1/p is nonzero and sqrt(p) is taken at a positive input.
The statement uses Real.rpow for both exponentiations, so it is specifically a real-power formulation.

No measurability, integrability, finiteness, or probability-space hypothesis is explicitly quantified; those facts are not premises of the proposition, and the integral is Mathlib's total Bochner-integral operation.
The measure is fixed specifically as gaussianReal(0,1); the statement does not quantify over Gaussian locations, scale parameters, or arbitrary random variables.
The target encodes only an upper bound. It does not encode a matching lower bound, an optimal or universal numerical value of C, or equality/asymptotic equivalence.
If the assumption p >= 1 were false, the implication for that p would be vacuous, but every eligible p is covered nonvacuously by the conclusion.
ambiguities: The dossier gives gaussianReal through gaussianPDF but does not include the definition of gaussianPDF, so the precise conventional interpretation of its second parameter (for example, variance versus another scale convention) cannot be recovered from the supplied material alone; it is safest to call it the nonnegative Gaussian parameter 1.
